summary.text: Bill Folden is a Republican Maryland state senator from District 4 in Frederick County who has held the seat since January 2023 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A U.S. Army veteran, he has worked in law enforcement as a Frederick County deputy sheriff and as a police officer.

paragraphs.text: William G. Folden was born in Hagerstown, Maryland, on April 5, 1972, and graduated from Governor Thomas Johnson High School in Frederick.
He earned an A.A. in criminal justice from Frederick Community College in 1999 and attended the School of Police Staff and Command at Northwestern University.
Folden served in the U.S. Army as a military police soldier and infantry sniper.

He was a Frederick County deputy sheriff from 1994 to 2011, a Frederick police officer from 2011 to 2022, and assistant chief of police for the University of Maryland, Baltimore, Police Department from 2022 to 2025.
Folden assumed office in the Maryland State Senate on January 11, 2023, succeeding Michael Hough.
According to the General Assembly website, he serves on the Judicial Proceedings Committee.
